shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-24 bug records. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,800 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED. **250 tier VERIFIED (#236); 190x5 VERIFIED (#237-#240).**
**✅ §24b VERIFIED IN PLAY (#240): rock now renders at every level, with Better Mountains installed.** Took three attempts; the failure chain is the most instructive record in this document.
UNVERIFIED: below-snow (needs a COLD map), depth shrink, camera anchor, §18 audit, reroll grid, VEE compat, GL roof fix.

**PUBLISHED-BUILD BUGS.** 1. Preview 190-only - **FIXED** (§6d-CLAMP). 2. Fog/rocks on reload - **HELD** (§21). 3. GL rivers - **TABLED with a contradiction** (§22). 4. MO formations 4x overlapping - **FIXED** (§24a). 5. Rock visible only one level down - **FIXED + VERIFIED** (§24b).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, gutter between. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter)/64)*64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position).

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** Path grid is IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH dimensions is distorted - a bug class that cannot appear on a square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, seven shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; random/edge cell; VEE Crater jitter | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); GL landform grids (§22) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge; river WIDTH | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |
| **Foreign absolute writes** (§22) | GL landform output lands in band 0, our carve overwrites it | ORDER, not arithmetic |

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).
**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for direct noise samplers.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells
**⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT BAND HEIGHT.** The original tiers were all 64k-2 - the tightest fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 ✅ |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** ✅ |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250/300 are vanilla's Medium and Large exactly. **Budget is tuned:** 192,000 = `3 x 64,000` = `2 x 96,000`. Ladder 7/5/3/2; 350/382 not offered because a second level exceeds the whole budget.
**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID** - just past the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.**
**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE** - "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" is the root of §15a and §4.
**Old saves are safe** - `bandHeight` is scribed; `SlotFor` is generic. **`Size.x == bandHeight` is a repair tool.**
**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES AND SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** Levels must be reduced BEFORE a larger size is selectable. Read the PLAN line before believing any size test.
**⚠ Own the widget, do not patch the data.** Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **the authoritative record of the choice.** **Adding a tier means growing the `InitialSize` postfix** (now +288f). **The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`.**

# 3-5. MOVEMENT, ORDERING, DESCENT
**Cross-band movement** segmented at ONE interception; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop UNTESTED IN PLAY.**
**Group ordering:** the drag line between bands runs through the GUTTER; the odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof - only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5.
**⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `TryResolveVisibleBelow`.** TEN systems share it. **NINE appearances of the single-step bug** - eight as `- Slot` arithmetic, **the ninth (§24b) as a TERRAIN-DEF GATE with no arithmetic in it at all**, invisible to the standing grep audit. **`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate.**

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Quantified (#237): surface 12,723 plants / fertility 0.631; +1 248 / 0.069; +2 170 / 0.046; +3 **37 / 0.012**.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` ports vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Confirmed three times: Water (§6b), Snow (§6f), **mass sprites (§24b)**.
**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS HANDLED.** A foreign `Thing.Print` postfix prints into OUR layer and is still correct, because the call is bracketed `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `Print` -> `FinishNewVerts`, and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE**. Preserve that.
**⚠ THREE DIFFERENT THINGS ARE ALL CALLED "MASS", AND THEY ARE REPRESENTED DIFFERENTLY.** This distinction cost three failed fixes (§24b):
| what | representation | drawn by |
|---|---|---|
| undug GROUND mountain | a real rock **edifice**, but FOGGED so its sprite is never printed | cap, from one Slot up |
| SKY-band mass | `AB_MountainTop` **terrain**, NO edifice at all | cap, into that band's own mesh |
| mined-out floor | rock leave-**terrain** | `ABMinedRockLookup` |
**Any code that tests only `edificeGrid` misses sky mass entirely; any code that tests only terrain misses undug ground.**
**⚠ THE CAP IS SINGLE-STEP.** `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from `-bands.Slot`, exactly one band down. Correct for a sky band's own tapering mass; the cost is that nothing else drew mass deeper than one slot until §24b.
**Ascent rule:** the dirty mirror stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell and its eight neighbours; the FIRST step stays unconditional *because* the cap is single-step.
**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.**

# 6b-6g. WATER, PREVIEW, COASTS, SNOW, SHRINK
**Water** is TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE; `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` targets `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`. Rivers remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`); `GetLakeCenter` needs the same or it undoes the first. Width clamped at the producer. **⚠ ALL THREE INERT UNDER GL** (§22).
**⚠ 6d-CLAMP, PUBLISHED BUG:** `Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `Clamp()`, which returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits*. Map Preview passes VANILLA's size (250 default), so `Clamp(250)` returned 190 **regardless of the player's pick**. **Fix: `PlannedSize`** - the chooser already wrote the answer to `GameInitData.mapSize`.
**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** With GL installed and Map Preview absent, `Active` is TRUE while window types are ABSENT. **Do not "simplify" `Active`.**
**6d-REROLL:** the window opened EMPTY - `elementSize.y = 403/126*896 = 2,866 px` -> `gridSize.y = 0` -> `DesiredCount = 0`.
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. NO SCALING. **⚠ "None override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.**
**Below-snow (UNVERIFIED):** no mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed. #237 showed it `finalized=False disabled=True` on a 14.6C map - plausible, needs a cold map.
**Depth shrink (UNVERIFIED):** **⚠ the atlas trap** - past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **⚠ natural rock excluded BY DEF, not by link type**, because BM makes rock non-linked.
**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.**

# 7-8a. CHARACTER, CAMERA
Ore `x(1+0.45*(depth-1))` scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`. **⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.**
**The camera clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`**, both per-frame paths where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into a hang.
**New-game anchor:** only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump. ⚠ OPEN: `z=24` was EXACTLY `PodScatterMargin`.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
Prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:`, two censuses. Has voided or explained six comparisons. **⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT AND SHOULD.**

## 9b. ⚠ "COST IS DESTRUCTION NOT GENERATION" - NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE FIX IS WHY
#188 was 16/84. #231 is 71/29. Rock suppression worked, so the carve got cheap and cost moved to generation. **A historical record of a fixed problem.**

## 9c-9f. Measured cost curve, five tiles
| run | plan | tile | gensteps | carve | total | destroyed | suppressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #231 | 7x126 | Flat TropSwamp | 3,836 | 1,580 | ~5.7 s | 4,575 | 1,627 |
| #236 | 3x250 | SmallHills | 5,001 | **7,118** | ~12.4 s | 15,611 | 7,272 |
| #237 | 5x190 | Mountainous | 4,529 | 2,201 | ~6.9 s | 7,497 | 85,304 |
| #238 | 5x190 | SmallHills | 3,389 | 4,718 | ~8.3 s | 16,100 | 11,175 |
| #239 | 5x190 | Mountainous Desert | 2,217 | 2,357 | **~4.7 s** | 7,906 | 76,702 |

**⚠ FillRock is SUPERLINEAR in band size:** 190 -> 36,480 cells -> ~1,250-2,200 ms; 250 -> 64,000 cells -> 4,254 ms. **1.75x cells, 2.87x time**, exactly as the `ListerThings` linear-`List.Remove` mechanism predicts.
**⚠ HILLINESS DECIDES THE BILL.** #237 vs #238 is a clean control - same tier, plan and biome, only hilliness differs - and the mountainous map SUPPRESSES 85,304 rocks while the small-hills map DESTROYS 16,100. Suppression is the cheap path.
**⚠ THE 250 TIER IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE** (~12.4 s vs ~4.7-8.3 s at 190). I recommended the 192,000 budget reasoning about PATHFINDING and did not predict generation time would double.

## 9g. ⚠ RE-RANKED ON EVIDENCE, AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE
`GenStep_Plants` across five tiles: **2,270 / 2,225 / 1,086 / 1,326 / 61.5 ms** - a **37x spread**, dominated by rainfall (Desert rain 378 -> 61.5 ms; TropicalSwamp rain 2693 -> 2,270 ms).
I made four successive wrong claims about this one number: *"84% is grown then erased"* (false - the `DESTROYED by def` census in the same log shows no plant def in the top ten; the cost is the SCAN, not wasted placement), *"biome-independent"* (dead at n=3), *"tracks hilliness"* (dead at n=4), *"1.1-2.3 s"* (dead at n=5).
**Basement `FillRock` is 1,250-4,254 ms on EVERY tile.** Tile-independent beats tile-dependent, so:
1. **Basement rock suppression** - consistently 1.2-4.3 s. **Now item 1.**
2. **`GenStep_Plants` traversal scoping** - 0.06-2.3 s, worthless on desert, ~2 s on wet flat. **Demoted.**
3. **`GenStep_RockChunks`** - `Filth_RubbleRock` is the top destroyed def on all five tiles.
4. Scattered ruins (also a CONTENT BUG). 5. Perlin precompute (changes determinism).

# 10-12. PERF AND DIAGNOSTICS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is in section-regeneration BURSTS.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST across runs.** Now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry. n=6.** Keep padding with a DISTINCT throwaway.
**⚠ THE AUTO-PROMPT IS EDGE-TRIGGERED, SO CHECK THE COUNT, NOT THE TEXT.** `monitor_get_error` returns the LATEST occurrence, which may be the FIRST - byte-identical and stale.
**⚠ Debug actions are `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`** - silently inert on the world map / preview screen.
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.** The below-layer report filtered on `StartsWith("SectionLayer_ABBelow")`, which excluded `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` - a layer that draws into the below view. **A missing row and an empty row are indistinguishable**, and the omission nearly cleared the guilty layer. Now `SectionLayer_AB`.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **§21 fog/rocks on reload** - the two-question observation. **Re-check now that §24b is fixed:** "rocks regenerate on reload" and "rock only draws one level down" could be the same report.
2. **Basement rock suppression** (§9g item 1).
3. Verify tiers 126/300; preview at 300; §18 audit; VEE compat; GL roof fix; reroll grid; depth shrink; camera anchor; below-snow (COLD map).
4. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report.
5. §9g items 2-5; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
6. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement.
7. `ShotReport` drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. Better Trees unexamined (§23c). **Store page still says three levels.**
8. **§22 TABLED** - do not resume without re-reading the contradiction.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Re-open a rejection only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ READ THE GUARD CLAUSES OF THE HELPER YOU ARE ABOUT TO REUSE - INCLUDING YOUR OWN.** §24b attempt 1 routed through `EmitMassSilhouetteAt` after reading only its SIGNATURE. Its body opens with three early returns, each of which independently disabled the fix: a mineable-edifice bail, a `!(g is Graphic_Linked)` bail, and its own hardcoded `-bands.Slot`. **I had this rule already and was applying it only to foreign code.**
**⚠ ASK HOW THE SUBSYSTEM REPRESENTS THE THING, NOT WHAT THE THING IS.** §24b attempt 2 assumed "mass" always means a rock edifice. Sky mass is `AB_MountainTop` TERRAIN with no edifice; undug ground mass is an edifice whose sprite is fogged; a mined floor is leave-terrain. **Three representations of one concept, and a test written against any one of them silently misses the others.**
**⚠ THE USER'S REPHRASING IS DATA.** "lower level textures disappear" and "+2 does not show the rock ledge of +1" describe the same screen but different mechanisms - the second names SKY mass specifically, which is what finally located the bug. **When a report is restated, diff the wording.**
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.** See §12.
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT.** #231's water report was clean and **worthless as a discriminator**: with `surfaceBand = 0`, "the river lands in band 0" and "the river lands on the surface" are THE SAME SENTENCE.
**⚠ A CENSUS BEATS A MAGNITUDE - AND I IGNORED MY OWN RULE.** The "84% of plant work is erased" claim came from a cell-count fraction while the census sat in the same log entry disagreeing with it.
**⚠ n=2 IS NOT A PATTERN, AND NEITHER IS n=4.** The plants number moved four times, each time breaking a claim I had just made from the previous sample. **On a multi-factor quantity, report the RANGE and stop naming drivers.**
**⚠ TILE-INDEPENDENT WINS BEAT TILE-DEPENDENT ONES.** Plants looked like the top optimisation at 2.2 s until a desert tile showed 61.5 ms. Basement rock is 1.2-4.3 s everywhere. **Rank by worst case across conditions, not by the best measurement you happen to have.**
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed - and RE-measure after.** Generation was 16% and is now 71% *because the fix worked*.
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE.** §21 named fog AND rocks and nothing else: exactly the two things stored as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`.
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** When a function's contract is "snap to something valid", it can never RECOVER a value.
**⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** All three original sizes were 64k-2; the real rule was only that *Slot* is 64-aligned.
**⚠ A RULE ENFORCED BY GREPPING A SYNTAX ONLY CATCHES THAT SYNTAX.** Eight `- Slot` bugs were found by grepping `- Slot`. The ninth was a terrain-def gate with no arithmetic in it.
**⚠ A DESIGN CHOICE RECORDED WITHOUT ITS COST WILL BE READ AS FREE.** "The cap derives from exactly one Slot below" sat in §6a as neutral architecture; it was also why rock vanished from +2.
**⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.** GL substitutes its own worker, so our patches never run - no error, no log line, no conflict warning.
**⚠ AND THE BUG AFTER THAT IS USUALLY A COLLABORATION.** Two locally-correct behaviours composing badly. **When neither side is wrong, look at the ORDER.**
**⚠ CHECK WHETHER IT IS ALREADY BUILT BEFORE BUILDING IT.** Two of three requested compat targets were already fully supported.
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** False-positive rate 50%; ReGrowth cleared four times.
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** **⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** **⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth.** **⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** **⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** **⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** **⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return.** **⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** **⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods.**
**Patching.** Re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the PRODUCER, not the store. Own the widget. Never put a foreign type in a patch signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **Prefix state is released in a Finalizer.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing it.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Prefer a published ExtensionPoint over racing internals.** **Read the LIVE def field, never a baked copy, when a mod can rewrite it at runtime.** **When a helper returns bool, use its return as the hand-off signal rather than duplicating its guards** (§24b).
**Engine facts.** `holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order is material render QUEUE, not altitude. `Banded` is FALSE for all of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses auto-discovered on EVERY map. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - generation latches must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` return silently unless `ProgramState == Playing`. Humanlikes past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED (~40x cheaper than after `FinalizeInit`).** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws but always runs FINALIZERS; **a prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN**; prefix and transpiler compose. **`FogGrid` and compressible things are flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`.** **`WaterInfo.GetWaterMovement` indexes `x * map.Size.z + z`.** **TileMutatorDefs compete within a `categories` entry, so a mod can REPLACE a vanilla mutator.** **`ThingDef.graphic` is baked at PostLoad and never refreshed; `graphicData.Graphic` is lazily rebuilt from CURRENT graphicData - which is why runtime retexture mods work at all.** **`subGraphic.MatSingle` of a linked graphic is the WHOLE atlas sheet; it is only ever valid through `MaterialAtlasPool.SubMaterialFromAtlas`.**

---

# 15-19. QOL / WEATHER / SETTINGS / AUDIT / FOREIGN MODLIST
**15a.** Nothing may exist in the void - finders answer inside the surface band; a `GenSpawn.Spawn` prefix rewrites `loc`; a 120-tick sweep catches teleports and pre-fix saves.
**15b.** `CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere. One prefix re-bases onto the band rect; eleven cold call sites inherit it. **ONE surface-edge finder**; a null dir means "any side, re-rolled" deliberately.
**15d.** Vanilla's no-build edge REMOVED - that strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge. **15e.** Drop pods fall through the levels.
**16.** `AB_OpenAir`/`AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`. Melt per band rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount` on EVERY call; **ReGrowth transpiles the same method and composes.** Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, a global Def. Readout rebuilt from `TryGetTemperatureForCell` - `OutdoorTemp` is NEVER reached because outdoor cells still belong to a Room.
**17.** **⚠ The blank-tab bug:** content height from the previous frame's `CurHeight` is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH without a floor. **⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.**
**18a.** State taken in a Prefix released in a Postfix - three instances; `ABAimAngle` swaps LIVE COMBAT STATE and opened with `patched = null`, DISCARDING a pending restore. All now `Finalizer`.
**18b.** The mirror: no `ProgramState` guard (~1.3M dead dispatches per 7-band carve), no ascent rule. **The mirror exists because of an earlier report of the §24b SYMPTOM** - "ground floor mineables disappear on floor 2" - caused then by stale meshes. **Same symptom, different cause; do not assume the mirror is at fault again.**
**18e. CLOSED:** `ABCavernGen.Generate` bails immediately without Biomes! Caverns. Re-confirmed #231, #237, #239.
**19.** The 910-mod failure was **not us** - the NRE is thrown while EVALUATING ARGUMENTS to `GenerateMap`. Real cause 24 lines earlier: a NEGATIVE `startingPawnCount`; exactly two mods patch it.

---

**We load at #900, LAST.** Harmony precedence is by PRIORITY, not load order.

## 20b. SHIPPED
1. **`Patch_VEE_LoneIsland_ABBandLocal`** - their falloff centres on `map.Center` and both passes walk `map.AllCells` writing elevation 0 + deep ocean below 0.2, so **every band except the middle becomes ocean, including the surface**. UNVERIFIED.
2. **`Patch_VEE_Crater_*`** - wraps the three private noise fields in `BandLocalModule`. ⚠ x jitter compresses too. UNVERIFIED.

4. **`Patch_GL_ABLandformRoofScope` + `Patch_RoofGrid_ABLandformSurfaceOnly`** - GL's roof sweep is ~800k `SetRoof` calls stamping surface roofs onto every band. UNVERIFIED.

## 20c. CLEARED - do not re-flag without a new confound
ReGrowth wall-snow (vertex range); ReGrowth `Printer_Plane` (linked graphics only); ReGrowth `IsSaveCompressible` + `Mineable.ExposeData` (**`IsSpaceRock()`-gated**); GL `AdjustMineables`; GL priority 800; ReGrowth `DoCellSteadyEffects`/`GetDrawParms`/`GenSpawn.Spawn`; VEE's river family and wildlife mutators.

# 21. ⚠ OPEN: FOG AND ROCKS ON SAVE RELOAD (HELD)
**ELIMINATED:** `ABV2.*` leakage; save compressibility; roof collapse; `RebindAfterLoad` ordering; ReGrowth (space-rock-only); Alpha Biomes / Biomes! (no save-path hooks).
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM PAIR POINTS AT US.** Fog and natural rock are exactly the two things stored as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`.
**⚠ RE-CHECK AGAINST §24b FIRST.** "Rocks regenerate on reload" and "rock only draws one level down" are indistinguishable if the player changed level between observations. §24b may have already fixed this.
**⚠ ONE LOAD, TWO QUESTIONS:** click a reappeared rock (selectable -> data, not -> rendering); check a player-built wall nearby (intact -> array desync, disturbed -> generation re-ran).

# 22. ⚠ TABLED: GL RIVERS
**Tabled with an unexplained contradiction, NOT resolved.**
**Confirmed:** GL REPLACES vanilla river generation (`GL_River` etc. are `TileMutatorDef`s in the `River` category on `TileMutatorWorker_Landform`). **#231: `riverGraph: 0 node(s)`.** Every river patch we own is **inert** under GL.
**The contradiction:** (1) `surfaceBand=0` -> river present in band 0; (2) later, no river anywhere, UNMEASURED; (3) later still, "rivers seem to work now", also unmeasured. **No code changed between 2 and 3.**
**Model that fit 1+2:** GL writes to roughly map rows 0-249 (`LandformGridSize` defaults to a square 250; `MapSpaceToNodeSpaceFactor` enters `GridFunction.Transform<double>` as a UNIFORM scalar). With a basement, band 0 is doomed and `FillRock` overwrites terrain unconditionally.
**Fix surface if resumed:** `TransformIntoMapSpace` is the one funnel but returns `IGridFunction<T>`, a foreign generic interface. `LandformGridSize` is published but sets RESOLUTION, not placement. **Worth contacting the GL author.**
**CLOSED red herring:** GL's `ApplyWaterFlow` indexes `i * map.Size.z + j`, matching vanilla's `GetWaterMovement`.

# 24. MULTI-CELL AND MULTI-LEVEL MASS

## 24a. FIXED: MO formations drawn four times overlapping
`IsPrintAnchor` picks the first cell of a multi-cell thing whose viewing cell can see it - single-valued **only if every cell resolves to the same `drop`**. It does not: `drop` comes from `TryResolveVisibleBelow` PER VIEWING CELL. Four cells, four anchors, four quads at the same `TrueCenter` - hence *overlapping*, not offset.
**Fixed by deduping per THING per Regenerate pass**, not by changing the anchor rule: the rule has a real job (a thing whose origin cell is hidden but whose far corner is visible must still draw). **Never MO-specific** - any 2x2+ thing was exposed.

## 24b. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED (#240): rock renders at every level
**Symptom:** with Better Mountains, rock was visible only ONE level below the viewer. At +1 it rendered but the colour shifted; at +2 the ground's rock was gone; at +3 the +1 ledge was gone. Terrain, trees and grass kept rendering at every depth - **only rock mass vanished.**

**Root cause, three layers deep:**
1. `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from `-bands.Slot`, exactly one band down, and draws into that band's OWN mesh - invisible from any other level.
2. `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2`'s bridge to it fired only for `def == AB_MountainTop`, so ordinary ground rock never matched.
3. Every cross-level path that DID exist ran through `EmitMassSilhouetteAt`, which returns false for mineable edifices and for non-linked graphics - **i.e. for every rock under BM**. That third guard is why the bug was BM-only.

**Fix:** a new `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap.EmitMassRepresentationAt` that draws the mass itself rather than its outline - rough-terrain field plus the sprite in whichever mode the def is in (`Graphic_Random` variants via the cap's own `StableCellIndex` so columns do not reshuffle between levels; atlas tiles with a neighbour mask derived from the ground map for vanilla linked rock). It is reached two ways:
- **unfogged sky ledges:** `if (!EmitMassSilhouetteAt(...)) EmitMassRepresentationAt(...)` - **using the silhouette's own bool return as the hand-off**, so vanilla linked rock keeps its lip and corner fillers and only declined cases fall through. No double draw.
- **fogged undug ground mountain:** called from the `foggedBelow` branch, gated `drop > slot` so the cap's territory at +1 is provably untouched.
`MassRockAt` resolves both representations: an edifice when there is one, else `AB_MountainTop` terrain typed from one Slot below exactly as the cap does.

**⚠ THREE FAILED ATTEMPTS, AND THE PATTERN IS THE VALUE.** Each failure was the same error in a different place - assuming how a subsystem represents mass instead of checking. (1) Reused a helper having read only its signature. (2) Assumed mass always means a rock edifice; sky mass is terrain. (3) Only the third attempt covered both representations. The lessons are in §14 under *read the guard clauses* and *ask how the subsystem represents the thing*.
